Visible and hidden paragraphs

The study of marine bioluminescence has long fascinated biologists and oceanographers alike. Deep-sea creatures from anglerfish to firefly squid produce cold light through a chemical reaction between luciferin and the enzyme luciferase. This eerie glow serves purposes as varied as attracting prey, signalling potential mates, and confusing predators in the perpetual darkness of the ocean floor.

Researchers using remotely operated vehicles have catalogued hundreds of species capable of producing light, yet the biochemical pathways involved differ dramatically between taxa. Unlike terrestrial fireflies, many deep-sea species cannot synthesise their own luciferin and must obtain it through diet, creating dependencies between predator and prey that ripple upward through the food chain.

This paragraph is hidden with display:none applied via a CSS class. ParagraphGroup must exclude it because getComputedStyle reveals display none even though no inline style is present. A word must never be hidden here.

This paragraph is hidden with visibility:hidden via a CSS class. It occupies layout space but is not visible to the player. ParagraphGroup must detect this through getComputedStyle and skip it entirely.

Screen-reader-only text. The bounding box is 1 × 1 px and the clip rule hides it visually. The bbox guard (width < 4 && height < 4) must exclude this element from any group, even though it has non-empty text content.
